title: Uniswap v3 withdrawal limits meter only decreased principal, so fees collected in the same call pass unmetered
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.5.2.2 closes with a scoping rule that is easy to read past: "These limits meter only the amount returned by decreasing liquidity. Fees already accrued on the position are collected in the same call but are not counted against them."

A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.5.2.3 shows why fees are unavoidably in the transaction. Before decreasing liquidity the Facet collects accrued fees, then decreases, then collects a second time — and "this second collection is what delivers the withdrawn principal to the ALM Proxy." The two collections are structurally required by how Uniswap v3 credits withdrawn amounts as tokens owed rather than transferring them.

The exclusion is defensible on purpose: a withdrawal rate limit exists to bound how fast a position can be unwound, and yield already earned is not exposure being unwound. Metering it would make the limit shrink for reasons unrelated to risk.

The consequence is that the token flow out of a position can exceed the metered amount, by an amount equal to accumulated fees. Anyone reconciling on-chain movements against consumed rate limits will find a systematic gap, and any monitoring that treats the limit as an upper bound on token inflow to the ALM Proxy is measuring the wrong quantity. It also creates a small structural incentive to leave fees uncollected as unmetered withdrawal headroom.
description: A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.5.2.2 excludes already-accrued position fees from the withdrawal rate limit even though the same transaction collects them and delivers them to the ALM Proxy.
